walkthroughs.body_html:
Textiles — a core area of GCSE Art & Design.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Textiles brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Textiles.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which technique uses crossing lines for tone?
options: Stippling
Cross-hatching
Smudging
Tracing
Lines
Dots
Circles
Squares
An unbalanced composition.
Painting in an old-fashioned style.
A composition with no balance.
Visual equilibrium achieved with different elements of equal visual weight on each side.

mcqs.q: What is appropriation in postmodern art?
options: Painting in an old-fashioned style.
Colours used to flatter the artist.
Deliberately reusing existing images or styles, often to comment on originality.
Stealing artwork to sell.
Painting in an old-fashioned style.
Colours opposite each other on the colour wheel that create strong contrast.
Colours that look similar and harmonise gently.
Colours used to flatter the artist.
